scope: Private local source-map transfer, publication and Mix authorization custody with synthetic inputs.

observations: The actual Elixir entry script filled a constrained Unix socket with part of a synthetic map. The owning BEAM process was suspended while the peer drained those bytes. The test observed a writable notification queued before allowing the writer to resume after the earlier grant cutoff. The peer then received EOF with zero additional bytes.
The receiver refused expired, misordered and oversized headers before requesting the body. The receiver and publisher also refused expiry during receipt and publication permission.

Directed SIGINT before authorization response, during Popen handle handoff and after successful direct-child reap returned 130 with group absence observed. Injected EPERM during group observation returned 2 with the Mix PID and direct-child reap state and blocked publication.

signed_postgresql.result: 1 passed, 12 excluded in an ACL-free temporary APFS checkout
observations: The signed owner fixture observed the earlier owner-grant cutoff at the publisher and the unchanged stored retention timestamp on success. The export matched the signed map bytes. Existing owner, signature, no-clobber, ACL, expiry and purge checks passed.
The first run from the normal checkout refused output because a home-directory ancestor had an ACL. The corrected run used a fresh ACL-free path and the same output ACL checks.

The marker and its hex form were absent from PostgreSQL and Mix logs. The TLS fixture recorded 20 peer closures and zero active connections. PostgreSQL exited 0 with its group gone, the port could be rebound, and the disposable checkout and PostgreSQL scratch were removed.

limits: The launch control delayed delivery of a real handle to the foreground. It did not exercise a stuck OS spawn.
Custody observations cover the isolated Mix process group. Detached descendants, forced foreground termination, Linux and host loss were outside these runs.

Expiry checks occur in userspace before send attempts and rename authorization. Descheduling between a check and a syscall remains possible. Buffered bytes and an authorized rename can complete later. Clock sampling and elapsed time follow the host and runtime clocks.
